newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine PM says recommends changes to banking laws.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine PM says recommends changes to banking laws.

text.p: The Ukrainian government has recommended a series of proposed changes to laws regulating banking, Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko told parliament.
"Not everything is going well in the banking sector, and we have to correct the situation quickly," Lazarenko said on Thursday.
Lazarenko did not provide details of changes to the laws.
But he criticised banks' credit policies, saying long-term loans accounted for only five percent of their activities.
"The absolute majority of banks made fast money on inflation, and development halted there," he said.

He also said half of Ukraine's money at the end of 1996 was in the shadow economy, compared to 25 percent at the start of 1995. Western economists estimate that the shadow economy accounts for up to 40 percent of economic activity.
The prime minister last week said he planned to head a special commission to oversee central bank activities, but the bank responded by saying the move would be illegal.
